Nexperia will help with chip testing. Fujifilm will start making semiconductor materials locally. Merck will supply very pure chemicals needed for chip production. These partners come from Europe, Japan, Singapore, and India. 

India government has received between $11 and $12 billion in proposals from companies that want to be part of semiconductor supply chain here. Each deal brings capability India did not have before

TDPowerSystems has received a new order worth approximately ₹192 crore through its US subsidiary, TDPS USA.

The order is from a leading multinational corporation for the supply of TDPS designed 2 Pole generators used in gas turbine applications. These generators will be installed in the United States, with deliveries scheduled between August 2027 and January 2028.

This is not just another order. The real significance lies in the type of product being supplied.TD Power has won the order using its own in house 2 Pole generator design. Developing and qualifying such generators requires deep engineering expertise, years of experience and customer approvals. Not many companies globally have these capabilities.

Management itself has called this a significant entry into the global 2 Pole generator market.

TD Power is therefore gradually moving up the value chain. Instead of being only a supplier of conventional generators, it is now winning orders in specialized high speed generator applications linked to gas turbines. These are technically demanding products where competition is much lower than in standard industrial generators.

If this project is executed successfully, it can become a strong reference project for future global customers.

When a large multinational corporation places a ₹192 crore order, it is effectively validating TD Power's technology, manufacturing quality and execution capabilities.
Large global customers usually spend months or even years evaluating suppliers before awarding such contracts.

Winning the first large order is often the hardest part. Once proven, repeat orders become easier to secure.

This order also indicates that TD Power is becoming relevant in the global 2 Pole generator market.
The company has previously indicated that the global generator opportunity is significantly larger than the domestic market. Success in this segment could open doors to many more international projects over the next several years.
This is particularly important because exports generally carry better margins and higher profitability compared to many domestic projects.

The order value of ₹192 crore is substantial relative to TD Power's size.
Since deliveries are scheduled between August 2027 and January 2028, this order provides revenue visibility for future periods and strengthens the order book. It also improves confidence in management's plans to increase manufacturing capacity towards ₹3,200 crore revenue capability and eventually beyond ₹4,000 crore.

The ₹192 crore value is important, but the strategic significance may be even bigger than the order size itself.
This order suggests that TD Power is successfully entering a specialized global generator segment where technological barriers are higher and competition is lower. If execution is successful, it could lead to repeat orders, stronger export growth, better margins and a larger share of the global generator market over the coming years.

Cabinet Approval for Four Textile Schemes Likely Soon: Industry Targeted to Reach $350 Billion by 2030 and $2.4 Trillion by 2047

Approval Timeline
The Union Cabinet is expected to approve four key components of the integrated programme for the textile sector announced in the Union Budget in the next two months, Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh said on Thursday

"In one or two months our entire scheme will be approved by the Cabinet," Singh said at a textile conclave organised by Laghu Udyog Bharati (LUB), a grassroots organisation representing MSMEs

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the integrated programme for the labour-intensive textile sector in her 2026-27 Budget speech

The programme comprises five sub-components, requiring individual Cabinet approvals for resource allocation and finalisation of operational details

The Schemes
National Fibre Scheme (NFS): will promote self-reliance in natural, man-made and new-age fibres, providing an umbrella framework for existing programmes such as the textile PLI scheme and Kasturi Cotton Bharat

Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme (TEEM): will support modernisation of traditional textile clusters through machinery and technology upgrades and common testing and certification facilities

Tex-Eco: will focus on making Indian textiles and apparel globally competitive and sustainable

Samarth 2.0: will upgrade the sector's skilling ecosystem through greater industry and academic collaboration

Domestic Manufacturing Push
Singh said India would soon begin domestic production of industrial stitching machines, which are currently largely imported

"A Taiwanese company is putting up a facility near Coimbatore which will start production soon," he said, signalling an effort to deepen domestic manufacturing capabilities in textile machinery

Credit Availability
The textiles ministry also held discussions with the Department of Financial Services to improve credit availability for the sector

"After the meetings credit flow to the units in the sector has started to improve gradually," he said

Long-Term Targets (Viksit Bharat 2047)
Industry size: from around $190 billion currently to $350 billion by 2030 and $2.4 trillion by 2047

Textile exports: from around $40 billion currently to $100 billion by 2030 and $600 billion by 2047

Core Theme
The government expects Cabinet approval within one to two months for the key components of its Budget-announced integrated textile programme, covering fibre self-reliance (NFS), cluster modernisation (TEEM), global competitiveness and sustainability (Tex-Eco) and skilling (Samarth 2.0), alongside efforts to produce stitching machines domestically and ease credit, as part of a roadmap to lift the industry from about $190 billion to $350 billion by 2030 and exports from $40 billion to $100 billion.

Adani Green Expands Battery Storage Limit: Operational BESS Capacity Reaches 6.63 GWh, Over Half of India's Total; Firm Aims for 50 GWh in Five Years

The Milestone
Adani Green Energy (AGEL) has expanded its operational battery energy storage system (BESS) capacity to 6.63 GWh, taking its share to more than half of India's operational BESS capacity of about 12.6 GWh

The capacity has nearly doubled from 3.55 GWh in June 2026

AGEL has achieved almost 70% of its FY27 target of adding over 10 GWh of battery storage capacity

The milestone was reached within 14 months of commencing on-site BESS construction at Khavda, and the latest addition was commissioned within 10 months of construction starting

What the Capacity Can Do
The 6.63 GWh BESS at Khavda, Gujarat, can store enough clean electricity to power around two million homes a day

It can support the peak electricity demand of cities such as Nagpur, Patna or Vizag for several hours

The company said the Khavda installation is the world's largest operational battery energy storage system at a single location

Integration and Technology
The facility is integrated with AGEL's renewable energy development at Khavda, where it is developing a 30 GW renewable energy plant across 538 sq km of barren land

The BESS uses lithium-ion battery technology, integrated with energy management systems and automated telemetry to manage charging and discharging, optimise system performance and support grid services

Battery storage helps manage peak demand, improve grid stability and reduce renewable energy curtailment

Future Plans
AGEL is targeting 50 GWh of storage capacity over the next five years and is also pursuing pumped-storage projects as part of its plan to build firm and dispatchable renewable power capacity

Sagar Adani, executive director, Adani Green Energy: "Reaching 6.63 GWh of operational battery storage in just 14 months is a significant milestone for AGEL and India's clean energy transition"

"At this scale, storage can make renewable power firmer, more reliable and dispatchable when the grid needs it"

"As India's power demand grows, we will continue to scale energy storage solutions, both battery and pumped storage, to support a more resilient, lower-carbon grid"

Core Theme
Adani Green has nearly doubled its operational battery storage to 6.63 GWh at Khavda, the world's largest single-location BESS and over half of India's total, reaching almost 70% of its FY27 target of adding 10 GWh in record construction time, as it pursues a 50 GWh goal over five years, backed by battery and pumped-storage projects, to make its renewable power firmer, more dispatchable and grid-ready.

UPI Continues to Grow Strongly, Volumes Up 23%: 24.07 Billion Transactions Worth ₹29.37 Trillion in September 2026

Year-on-Year Growth
UPI volumes grew 22.6% YoY to 24.07 billion in September 2026, from 19.63 billion in September 2025

Value of transactions grew 18% to ₹29.37 trillion, from ₹24.89 trillion in September 2025

Month-on-Month Dip
UPI volumes declined 1.8% from 24.51 billion in August, partly because September had 30 days compared with 31 days in August

Transaction value fell 1.5% to ₹29.37 trillion from ₹29.82 trillion in the previous month

The dip is not unusual: 10 of the past 24 months (including September) saw a low single-digit (1.0 to 2.3%) MoM decline in volumes due to fewer days

On three instances, the decline was between 5.2% and 6.7%; two were in February (2025 and 2026), which have 2-3 days fewer than January, and one was in November 2024, attributed to Diwali being in October 2024

The last 30-day month, June, saw 22.72 billion transactions worth ₹28.92 trillion

Daily Averages
UPI clocked its highest average daily transaction volume of 802 million payments in September

Average daily value of all transactions was ₹97,913 crore in the same month

In June, daily transactions were 757 million, with a value of ₹96,405 crore

Festive Season and MDR
Reeju Datta, cofounder of Cashfree: "This rise came from the start of the festive season. Ganesh Chaturthi fell in mid-September this year, and people began spending on festivities"

From April to August, the money moving through UPI each day had stayed at around ₹96,000 crore even as payments grew, because most new payments were small

Trade groups had previously raised concerns over the introduction of the merchant discount rate (MDR), ending six years of zero-charge UPI transactions

Effective October 15, the NPCI will introduce an MDR structure for select UPI payments

Core Theme
UPI continued its strong run in September 2026, with volumes up 22.6% to 24.07 billion and value up 18% to ₹29.37 trillion YoY and record daily volumes of 802 million payments on the back of early festive spending, while the small MoM dip is a calendar effect, with the bigger change ahead as NPCI introduces an MDR structure on select UPI payments from October 15, ending six years of zero-charge transactions.

Anup Saha Is New Kotak Bank MD & CEO: Three-Year Term Begins January 1, 2027, Ending Leadership Uncertainty

The Appointment
Kotak Mahindra Bank Whole-time Director Anup Saha will be managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) of the lender for a term of three years

The bank said on Thursday that the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) had given its nod to the appointment, effective January 1, 2027

Saha, 56, is executive director overseeing retail banking, data analytics and marketing

The approval ends the leadership uncertainty at the bank since incumbent MD & CEO Ashok Vaswani announced his exit in June

In June, the bank had said Vaswani would not seek reappointment due to personal reasons when his term ended in December; he assumed office on January 1, 2024, for a three-year term

Saha joined the bank in January this year

He could serve until he turns 70, subject to approval by the board and RBI, providing a longer leadership horizon for strategic and operational changes

Saha's Statement
"I look forward to working with my colleagues to deepen customer relationships, tirelessly execute and build sustainable value for shareholders and all our stakeholders"

"We will remain firmly focused on doing the right thing and getting it right by the customer"

Analyst Views
Citi: the decision delivers strategic continuity while installing a retail/consumer banking-focused leader at the helm; constructive on two counts, reaccelerating growth and easing the overhang of capital deployment

Other brokerages see Saha's key priorities as stabilising the organisation and stemming senior-level exits, accelerating balance-sheet growth to improve return on equity (RoE), building a more granular liabilities franchise, and improving turnaround time and responsiveness across the bank

Suresh Ganapathy, MD & head of India research, Macquarie Capital: "The single-biggest priority is to drive loan growth and deposit growth." Kotak's RoE is the lowest among its large peers, and the only way to improve it is to consume more capital and drive up leverage through faster balance-sheet growth

Another priority is making the deposit base granular, as deposits above ₹5 crore formed almost 23% of the balance sheet as of June 2025, and he would look to see this proportion coming down

Jefferies: Saha has experience leading the retail segment at Bajaj Finance and ICICI Bank; timely team reorganisation, if any, will help; "an uptick in the bank's retail deposit and net interest income (NII) growth, along with operational efficiencies, can lift earnings"

Saha's Background
Over 32 years' professional experience, including 25 years in financial services across banking and non-banking financial institutions

Associated with Bajaj Finance, the largest private sector NBFC, from 2017: roles from president (consumer finance), followed by deputy CEO (consumer; MSMEs; marketing; operations and service; digital platform), executive director, deputy MD, and finally MD & CEO from April 2025 until his resignation in July the same year

14 years at ICICI Bank, as senior general manager and group product head overseeing retail home loans, vehicle loans, developer funding and the credit-card business

GE Capital from 1999 to 2003 (credit cards, sales and analytics) and Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd from 1991 to 1995 (production engineering, then a brief stint in sales of consumer durables)

Alumnus of IIT Kharagpur and IIM Lucknow

Core Theme
Kotak Mahindra Bank has named Anup Saha, a retail-focused executive with experience at Bajaj Finance, ICICI Bank and GE Capital, as MD & CEO for a three-year term starting January 1, 2027, ending the leadership uncertainty since Ashok Vaswani's exit announcement. Analysts expect strategic continuity with a push on loan and deposit growth, a more granular liabilities franchise, stabilising the senior team and lifting the bank's return on equity, currently the lowest among large peers.

INDIA IPO MARKET | RECORD H1 FY27 FUNDRAISING

Fundraising Surge
- Mainboard + SME IPOs crossed ₹1 lakh Cr.
- H1 FY27 fundraising grew ~31% YoY.
- Mainboard IPOs raised ₹94,205 Cr.
- Mainboard fundraising increased 35% YoY.
- 78 mainboard issues came to market.

Deferred IPOs
- Several deferred IPOs finally entered the market.
- SEBI's one-time extension expired September 30.
- NSE, SBI Funds Management and Manipal Health boosted fundraising.
- Large issues materially lifted overall numbers.

Investor Participation
- Strong SIP flows support primary-market demand.
- Retail participation remains an important capital source.
- FPI activity shows a contrasting pattern.
- FPIs invested ₹44,960 Cr in primary issues.
- FPIs sold ₹1.64 lakh Cr in secondary markets.

IPO Listing Gains
- 64 IPOs had available listing data.
- Average listing gain reached ~19%.
- H1 FY26 average listing gain was ~7%.
- Strong listings can support investor participation.
- Higher participation can encourage further IPO launches.

Fresh Capital vs OFS
- Fresh capital stood at ₹38,510 Cr.
- Fresh capital represented ~41% of mainboard proceeds.
- Large proceeds came through OFS.
- Promoters and PE/VC investors monetized holdings.
- Government disinvestment also contributed significantly.

OFS Fundraising
- H1 FY27 OFS fundraising reached ₹55,337–67,382 Cr.
- Range varies by segment and data definition.
- Fundraising was significantly higher than last year.
- Government disinvestment was a major contributor.

IPO Pipeline
- ~145 SEBI-approved companies await launch.
- Potential fundraising stands at ₹2.78 lakh Cr.
- Another 102 companies await approval.
- Their potential fundraising stands at ~₹1.87 lakh Cr.
- Overall supply pipeline remains substantial.

SME IPO Segment
- SME subscription metrics have weakened.
- SME fundraising is lower versus last year.
- Investor selectivity appears higher among smaller issuers.
- Quality and valuation remain important considerations.

Primary Market Shift
- India's primary market is becoming a liquidity destination.
- SIP flows provide recurring equity-market capital.
- IPO listings can reinforce investor participation.
- Strong participation encourages more companies to raise capital.

H2 FY27 Outlook
- IPO activity could remain elevated.
- Large pipeline increases potential equity supply.
- Quality and valuation may become increasingly important.
- Earnings visibility could matter more for issuers.
- Crude and bond yields remain external variables.
- FPI flows could influence overall market conditions.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India's primary market has entered a record fundraising phase, with H1 FY27 IPOs crossing ₹1 lakh Cr. However, only ~41% of mainboard proceeds represented fresh capital, while the large IPO pipeline could make H2 FY27 increasingly quality- and valuation-driven.

India’s passenger vehicle market is showing a strong recovery. Domestic PV sales jumped 21.4% YoY to 4.63 lakh units in September 2026, helped by festive demand, GST 2.0 and a favourable low-base effect. 

Maruti led the growth with sales up 36.9%, while Tata Motors, Mahindra and Hyundai also posted double-digit growth.

The recovery isn’t limited to one segment. 

SUV demand remains strong, but smaller cars are also making a comeback, with improved affordability after GST 2.0 supporting demand. 

The bigger question now is whether this momentum sustains after the festive season, especially as the industry enters a tougher base from October.

For auto investors, the next few months will be important to watch - volumes, discounts, inventory levels, SUV vs hatchback mix and the sustainability of the demand recovery will tell us much more than one strong month.

AEQUS | THE $1 BN BACKLOG HIDES THE REAL STORY

Aerospace Capacity Expansion
- Aerospace order book exceeds $1 Bn.
- Top-line growth stands at ~38%.
- New capex cycle totals $350–400 Mn.
- Hosur facility anchors the expansion.
- Expansion targets higher aerospace manufacturing capacity.

Margin Geographic Arbitrage
- Strategy involves shifting complex manufacturing to India.
- Capabilities include aero-engine components and landing gears.
- Technology is being transferred from French facilities.
- India offers significant manufacturing cost advantages.
- Current aerospace EBITDA margin is ~33%.
- Successful execution could support sustained margins.

Value-Chain Expansion
- AEQUS historically operated as a build-to-print supplier.
- Products include LCA pylons and Airbus wheels.
- Strategy is moving toward system-level integration.
- New JVs support UAV development.
- Technology transfers are being pursued.
- UAVs target India's defence sector.
- Opportunity extends into avionics and software.

Consumer Segment
- Consumer electronics and toys remain underutilized.
- Current capacity utilization is ~31%.
- Segment currently weighs on consolidated profitability.
- PAT breakeven is expected around FY28.
- India-Europe FTA could improve export economics.
- Europe-bound toy and electronics exports could scale.
- Utilization target is ~80%.

Key Execution Question
- Multiple operational transitions must execute together.
- Factory expansion alone does not ensure returns.
- Technology transfer requires successful execution.
- System integration requires new capabilities.
- Consumer utilization must improve materially.
- Aerospace growth must convert into cash flows.

Working Capital Risk
- Aerospace growth can increase working-capital requirements.
- Long cash conversion cycles can pressure liquidity.
- Balance-sheet capacity remains an important variable.
- Timing of cash generation is critical.

₹650 Cr Warrant Issue
- Company recently approved a ₹650 Cr warrant issue.
- Capital raise adds funding for expansion.
- Equity dilution is an important consideration.
- Detailed dilution impact requires warrant terms.

KEY TAKEAWAY
AEQUS's story extends beyond its $1 Bn+ aerospace backlog. The strategy involves shifting complex manufacturing to India, moving toward system-level integration and improving consumer utilization. The key variables remain execution, working capital and the timing of cash generation.

• There will be no change in the shareholding patterns of Sunteck and Satguru.

reports.text:
CASHurDRIVE: Building an Advertising Layer on New-Age Transit Infrastructure

Cash Ur Drive Marketing Limited (CUDML) is expanding its OOH advertising network by securing commercial advertising and media rights across emerging transit infrastructure, without owning the underlying assets.

• Holds advertising/media rights across 1,900+ buses, ~500 EV charging stations, 19 battery swapping stations, 95+ digital screens and 350+ public bicycle shelters
• FY26 Revenue from Operations stood at ₹186.67 Cr, up 33.98% YoY, while PAT stood at ₹29.40 Cr, up 64.93% YoY
• Owned media revenue increased to ₹59.07 Cr in FY26 from ₹26.50 Cr in FY25 and ₹2.4 Cr in FY23
• Secured a 10-year EV charging concession in Rishikesh , Pune city bus advertising mandate and an exclusive agreement with Punbus covering 1,200+ state buses
• Entered EV charging and mobility infrastructure through acquisition of 50% in CharjKaro Greentech Mobility and ~ 19.06% in Kolkata Call Taxi
• Pan India Presence, with 2,000+ clients served
• FY26 revenue mix: Transit Media 44.84% and Outdoor, Urban Infrastructure Media 49.19% & with the balance from other segments 5.97%

Key takeaway: CASHurDRIVE is expanding its owned-media portfolio by monetising advertising rights across buses, EV charging, public mobility and urban infrastructure, while continuing to add new media inventory across India.

reports.text:
INDIA CNC MACHINING | SKILLED WORKFORCE + DEFENCE EXPORT OPPORTUNITY

CNC Adoption
- India continues importing more CNC machines.
- Machine availability is not the main constraint.
- Skilled operators remain critical for utilization.
- CNC adoption among small factories grew 18% in 2025.
- Switching costs are gradually declining.

Skilled Workforce Gap
- Aerospace and defence parts require precision machining.
- Every order can involve different specifications.
- Machinists select tools and adjust machine settings.
- Operators must monitor tool wear closely.
- Machines repeat programmed instructions.
- India trains ~68,000 machinists annually through ITIs.
- Source highlights a significant workforce requirement gap.

Small Factory Opportunity
- India has ~72 Mn small and medium factories.
- Rajkot and Ludhiana retain significant manual machining.
- Around 60–65% reportedly still use manual machines.
- CNC upgrades can improve manufacturing precision.
- Delayed adoption can affect competitiveness.

Government Support
- Government support can offset CNC transition costs.
- Factories may receive 4–6% of additional sales.
- Banks can finance up to 85% of machine costs.
- Small businesses can therefore access equipment financing.

Aerospace & Defence Demand
- European defence spending is increasing sharply.
- Europe remains dependent on defence imports.
- Aerospace and missile components require precision machining.
- European manufacturers need additional production capacity.
- Indian suppliers are receiving defence component orders.

India Defence Exports
- India's defence exports reached ₹21,000 Cr last year.
- Government targets ₹50,000 Cr by FY29.
- European defence demand creates export opportunities.
- Indian manufacturers are entering global supply chains.
- CNC machining remains critical for precision components.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India's CNC opportunity extends beyond machine sales. Skilled machinists, factory upgrades and precision manufacturing capacity are becoming increasingly important as aerospace and defence exports expand. The combination of CNC adoption and global defence demand could support India's precision-component manufacturing ecosystem.

India is buying 6 new submarines from Germany, This deal is worth about ₹70,000 crore

Germany won because its submarines can stay underwater for weeks without coming up to breathe. India tried to build this technology on its own through DRDO but could not get it ready even after 15 years of work. So now India is buying it from Germany instead. 

Germany also made it easier by removing many items from its export ban list. India still needs 1 final government approval before signing

Pakistan is getting 8 new submarines from China. 4 are already built and being tested right now in Chinese waters. They will join Pakistan Navy this year. India has 16 old submarines, most over 30 years old, and 3 more could retire soon. 

India new German submarines will not arrive before 2033 at best. So for next 7 years, Pakistan will have newer underwater boats while India waits for its order. This is why timing of this deal matters so much

Mazagon Dock, which builds these submarines in Mumbai, currently has orders worth ₹27,000 crore. This 1 deal alone would push their orders past ₹1,00,000 crore. 

But what is more interesting is who else benefits. Indian steel companies supply special submarine grade steel. Indian battery makers supply power units. Indian electronics firms build sonar and radar systems. 

So 1 big defence deal feeds work into dozens of Indian factories and engineers across different industries.

But Germany works with Turkey, and Turkey works closely with Pakistan on submarines. So there is fear some sensitive Indian submarine knowledge could indirectly reach Pakistan through shared companies, engineers, software or suppliers.

TKMS says this fear is exaggerated. Germany says it has become much stricter with Pakistan and China and has even blocked important submarine-related technology exports to them

The other side also has old links with Pakistan. France had earlier sold Pakistan Mirage jets and Agosta submarines, but later stopped direct military support as France became closer to India.

India is deciding not only which submarine is better, but also which foreign partner is safer and more trustworthy for secret submarine technology.
At the same time, Pakistan is buying 8 Chinese AIP submarines, so this deal is strategically very important for India.

INDIA'S MANUFACTURING PROBLEM | BUT CHANGE IS BEGINNING

R&D Investment Gap
- India spends <1% of GDP on research.
- South Korea spends nearly 5%.
- China spends around 2.4%.
- Private companies provide only 36% of research funding.

Corporate Capital Allocation
- Indian companies are generating record profits.
- Many prefer debt repayment over fresh factories.
- Buybacks and cash reserves remain preferred.
- Financial returns can look safer than manufacturing.
- Boardrooms often prioritize near-term profitability.

China+1 Shift
- Southeast Asia attracted $225 billion factory investment.
- Vietnam received ~$25 billion.
- Around 67% went toward factory projects.
- India received ~$39 billion overall.
- India's new factory projects reportedly fell sharply.

Why Southeast Asia Wins
- Vietnam offers faster delivery.
- Customs processes are considered smoother.
- Supply chains are more established.
- Manufacturing relocation isn't only about wages.
- Faster shipping can matter more than labour costs.

India's Talent Challenge
- Top engineering graduates often choose finance.
- Consulting also attracts engineering talent.
- Manufacturing careers receive comparatively less preference.
- Some industrial families are exiting factories.
- Capital is increasingly moving toward financial assets.

Manufacturing Share
- Manufacturing stayed around 14–17% of GDP.
- This pattern persisted for roughly three decades.
- Subsidies alone haven't transformed the share.
- Tax incentives haven't solved structural bottlenecks.

What Needs To Change
- More private R&D investment is needed.
- Faster project execution remains important.
- Logistics and customs need further improvement.
- Manufacturing needs stronger skilled talent.
- Long-term industrial capital must increase.
- Supply-chain depth needs continued development.

KEY TAKEAWAY
India has made progress, but manufacturing still needs structural reforms. R&D, logistics, supply chains, industrial talent and long-term private capital remain critical. The opportunity is changing, but sustained execution will determine whether India captures the next manufacturing cycle.

IPO Fee Pool
- Investment banks earned ₹2,274 Cr in Jan–Sep 2026.
- Fees came from 81 mainboard IPOs.
- Total IPO value reached ₹1.05 lakh Cr.
- Last year fees were ~₹2,238 Cr.
- Last year covered 74 IPOs.
- Last year's issue value was ₹85,256 Cr.

Biggest Fee Payouts
- NSE generated the highest fee at ₹186 Cr.
- NSE fee equaled ~0.82% of issue size.
- Manipal Health Enterprises paid ₹165.94 Cr.
- Dhoot Transmission paid ₹86 Cr.
- Fractal Analytics paid ₹71.1 Cr.
- Shadowfax Tech paid ₹70.37 Cr.
- Clean Max Enviro paid ₹67 Cr.

Highest Fee Ratios
- Fees ranged from 0.05% to 15.6%.
- SBI Funds Management paid just 0.05%.
- Innovision paid the highest at 15.6%.
- Average fees remained around 3–4%.
- MV Electrosystems paid ~8.3%.
- Skyways Air Services paid ~6.7%.
- Jindal Supreme India paid ~5.9%.
- Hy-Tech Engineers also had high fees.

Quarterly Fee Trend
- Q4 FY25: 9 IPOs, ₹406 Cr fees.
- Q1 FY26: 15 IPOs, ₹630 Cr fees.
- Q2 FY26: 50 IPOs, ₹1,202 Cr fees.
- Q3 FY26: 29 IPOs, ₹1,914 Cr fees.
- Q4 FY26: 18 IPOs, ₹577 Cr fees.
- Q1 FY27: 9 IPOs, ₹133 Cr fees.
- Q2 FY27: 54 IPOs, ₹1,564 Cr fees.

September Quarter
- September quarter saw ~₹1,600 Cr fees.
- 54 companies completed IPOs.
- IPO value reached ~₹83,200 Cr.
- It was the highest quarterly payout since Dec 2025.
- December 2025 quarter generated >₹1,900 Cr.
- That quarter had 29 IPOs worth ₹90,660 Cr.

Why Fees Vary
- Fee percentages depend on transaction structure.
- Fixed fees can inflate percentage ratios.
- Smaller IPOs can show higher fee percentages.
- Reported fees include 18% GST.
- GST should be netted when comparing fees.
- Deal complexity also affects fee structures.

KEY TAKEAWAY
Investment banks earned ₹2,274 Cr from 81 mainboard IPOs during Jan–Sep 2026. September-quarter activity drove a major portion of fees, while individual fee percentages varied sharply due to fixed-fee structures, GST and transaction complexity.

📈 𝘙𝘦𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘦𝘯𝘥𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯: BUY
🏛 𝘉𝘳𝘰𝘬𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘨𝘦: Motilal Oswal**

Motilal Oswal has reiterated its 𝗕𝗨𝗬 rating on Time Technoplast Ltd. with a 𝗧𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲𝘁 𝗣𝗿𝗶𝗰𝗲 (𝗧𝗣) 𝗼𝗳 ₹280, suggesting a potential upside of 54%. 📈

The brokerage firm highlights several key growth drivers and margin expansion opportunities for the company. FY26 is noted as the most successful year in Time Technoplast's history, with significant year-on-year (YoY) growth:

- 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲: Increased by ~12%
- 𝗘𝗕𝗜𝗧𝗗𝗔: Grew by ~14%
- 𝗣𝗔𝗧: Rose by ~21%

This strong performance was achieved despite a challenging operating environment characterized by geopolitical tensions and volatile commodity prices. The company's predominantly B2B model, coupled with a disciplined monthly pricing mechanism, allowed it to effectively pass on input cost fluctuations to customers, thereby protecting its margins. This positive momentum is expected to continue into FY27.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 & 𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗢𝘂𝘁𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸:

- 𝗩𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗺𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: Management is confident in achieving the guided 13-15% 𝘃𝗼𝗹𝘂𝗺𝗲 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵 in the medium term, with potential to even surpass this range. 💪
- 𝗠𝗲𝗿𝗴𝗲𝗿: The board will consider the merger of its ~75% subsidiary, TPL Plastech, with itself on September 29, 2026. This merger is expected to enhance operational efficiency. TPL Plastech reported FY26 revenue/PAT of ₹4.2 billion/₹2.9 billion.
- 𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝗣𝗹𝗮𝗻𝘁: A greenfield, fully automated plant using robotics has been commissioned in Bhilad, Gujarat, with a revenue potential of ₹1 billion for packaging products.
- 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘀𝗶𝘁𝗲 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀: The company continues to receive orders and explore opportunities, including a small order for hydrogen cylinders from NTPC's locomotive pilot project. 🚚

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.

Tata Group Boardroom Tug of War
Some history repeat; Some history rhyme
30 yrs ago it was Ratan Tata vs Russi Mody. Today, many see shades of that battle in the Chandra vs Noel Tata face-off
Back in the 1990s, Ratan Tata was consolidating authority within a sprawling Tata empire run by powerful Operating entity heads. Russi Mody was among the most influential Tata executives of his era. Larger-than-life personality, huge public profile & massive influence within the group.
Ratan Tata believed Tata Group needed one strategic centre of gravity. Not multiple power centres running individual fiefdoms. Eventually, Russi Mody exited & Ratan Tata tightened control over the conglomerate.
Fast forward three decades.
The debate is again centred around leadership, control & the future direction of Tata Sons. This time its Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, & N Chandrasekaran, who leads Tata Sons
Key contentions are Chandra’s reappointment as chairman & Tata Sons listing. Noel Tata has opposed both
The striking part? Tata Sons board backed Chandra by a 4:1 vote, while Noel Tata stood opposed
Russi Mody took the battle public. Media interviews, public sparring & headline-grabbing exchanges became part of the story.
Chandra, however, has largely stayed silent in public
Whether history repeats or merely echoes, one thing is clear
Generational change of Tata leadership eventually confronts the same question.

Is India investing enough for future capacity

India is usually described as a consumption economy. Consumption contributes >60% of GDP. But the story becomes incomplete when we ignore what's happening on the investment side and other aspects of our economy

India's Gross Capital Formation is ~32.6% of GDP. Lower than China's ~40%, but China's per capita GDP is several times of India's. Comparing ratios without considering income levels misses the context.

A developing country cannot allocate every ₹ toward factories & infra. A large share of resources must also support the bottom of the pyramid through housing, healthcare, education & welfare.

A harmonious society requires a minimum standard of living for those at the bottom. India is building capacity while simultaneously funding social stability. That's a tougher balancing act than many realize.

So let's move beyond GDP narratives & look at hard physical data. India's share of global GDP is only ~3.5% yet produces roughly 10% of the world's steel. Steel almost 3x our weight in global GDP. Steel isn't consumed for consumption's sake, but goes into factories, rail tracks, power plants, ports, airports, infrastructure etc

Cement tells the same story. India produces ~400 MT annually out of ~4,000 MT globally. Again, roughly 10% global share despite only ~3.5% share of world GDP. Countries don't consume steel & cement at this scale unless they are building physical assets. These are the raw materials of future GDP.

Power generation presents a slightly different picture. India's share of global electricity output is lower than steel & cement, but still materially ahead of its global GDP share. India with 1800bn units vs 32,000bn units, 6% global share

The evidence suggests India is investing for future capability. One may argue the investment cycle started later than it should have, but the direction is unmistakable. Steel, Cement & Power share point toward economy preparing for a much larger future.

The scale of projects are also changing. DFCs, industrial corridors, semiconductor fabs, renewable energy parks, metros, airports, transmission corridors & logistics networks are larger than anything India attempted before.

If this trend continues, India's share of global steel, cement & power usage is likely to keep rising. Higher material intensity today is often a precursor to higher economic output tomorrow.

Maybe the better way to describe India isn't "consumption economy." It's a country simultaneously consuming, uplifting millions & building future productive capacity. 
India need a balancing act of Building future and taking care of the needy, which it is working towards

De-Dollarization lets peek into central bank reserves

Central banks are diversifying but US$ isn't giving up the throne anytime soon. Headlines scream de-dollarization bt US$ still makes up ~57% of global FX reserves. That's down from decades ago, but still miles ahead of everyone else.

Euro is the 2nd largest reserve currency at ~20%. But Europe faces weak growth, aging demographics, fiscal stress & fragmented politics. Hence no comfort for people looking to diversify away from US$

Then its China. Despite its economic size, RMB is only ~2% of global reserves & ~2% of global payments. Clear reflection of trust issues with the dragon. deep capital markets, convertibility & rule of law issues also there

They're moving into something with no issuer at all: Gold. Central banks themselves are now one of the biggest sources of gold demand globally, roughly buy ~30% of annual global mine production

Gold isn't rising only because investors are bullish. Significant chunk of global prodn is locked away by sovereign balance sheets. In 2026, central banks gold buying at slower pace vs 2025 due to 60% price rise.

Among the Major buyers were Poland, China, Brazil, India etc. 
Then there are few sellers too. Turkey has been among the largest sellers this year, reportedly selling ~83t YTD to support liquidity & FX/US$ needs.

That’s the problem. Though world want to move away from US$ in the long term but  issue in the medium term created due to lack of US$ in the country. 
Case in point Turkiye

Russia has also been a notable seller, reducing reserves by ~44t YTD as it seeks hard-currency liquidity. But Russia is also large producer of Gold

Gold is becoming a reserve diversification asset in a world where trust in fiat issuers is fragmenting.
BUT de-dollarization in reserves doesn't mean de-dollarization in trade.
That’s two very different thing

Global trade still run on the USD infrastructure. That network effect is incredibly hard to replace.
So its two-step process. Trade continues in USD.
But exporting nations convert a portion of their accumulated surplus reserves into gold, commodities, sovereign funds or other reserve assets.

The world may keep transacting in dollars while increasingly choosing not to store all its savings in dollars.

Conclusion:
Real story is different from "the end of the USD."
Reserve diversification is real.
Dollar replacement is not. Not in near future

Birla trying to replicate Paint like disruption in Wire & Cables
India's W&C industry is a INR 1.1trn & growing at ~13% CAGR. Despite its size (0.3% of India GDP), industry remains fragmented with top 6 players control ~50% share

Market is roughly split into 3 equal buckets: Wires, LT Cables & MV/HT/EHV/Specialized Cables. Cables compared to wire is more organized, house wires have larger unorganized participation. Overall unorganized is > 30%

what attracted Birla. W&C sits at the intersection of electrification, urbanization & digitization. Housing, infra, renewables, data centres & manufacturing all need more wires.

Ultratech has launched Ultravolt with planned capex of ₹18 bn. Initial plant capacity has already started production ahead of schedule at Bharuch. The market compares this with the paint disruption. Lets look at numbers

Grasim's paint capex was ~65-70% of Asian Paint. Ultravolt's ₹18 bn capex is 30% of Polycab gross block. Plus, Polycab's gross block is expected to reach ~₹94 bn in FY28 while KEI could reach ~₹43 bn. Ultravolt's announced gross block is only ₹18 bn

The biggest advantage for Ultratech is raw material availability. Copper & Aluminium dominate industry economics and the Birla ecosystem already has deep expertise & inhouse production

Demand-intelligence advantage. Cement is purchased 6 months before wires in building construction. Ultratech can potentially spot demand trends 4-6 months ahead of competitors

Builder relationships, contractor network & Ultratech Building Solutions outlets create a ready-made ecosystem for cross-selling wires. That's a powerful advantage most new entrant

Ultravolt has prepared well. Better channel incentives, faster delivery commitments, aggressive marketing & strong retailer engagement are already creating buzz. But replicating the paint playbook won't be straightforward. 

Paints & cement share significant overlap in distribution. Wires are largely sold through electrical dealers, distributors, retailers & electrician networks. Building an electrical distribution franchise takes years

Another key difference is profitability. Leading W&C players operate at ~12-14% EBITDA margins, far lower than the 18-20%+ margins paint Co. enjoyed before disruption. With lower margins, room for aggressive pricing is limited

Further: Utility, industrial, railway, transmission & infra projects require extensive testing, approvals, certifications & execution history before meaningful scale can be achieved.
Conclusion: Birla has genuine advantage in raw material sourcing, builder relationships & demand visibility. But unlike paints, incumbents start with lower margins, stronger technical moats & entrenched distribution

Jury is still out. Ultravolt looks prepared. Space will remain interesting

Coforge Chairman resignation : Lets dig deeper

OP Bhatt's resignation came after disagreements around the Board evaluation process. In his resignation note, he says continuing on Board amid differences regarding his "good faith actions" would not be conducive to Board effective functioning 

OP Bhatt is not a conventional IT industry chairman. He is among India's most respected bankers, having led SBI between 2006-11 & later served on boards across large corporates including Tata Group companies

The market doesn’t take such update kindly, but Bhatt's continuation was already under question even before the resignation. Shareholders (inc largest shareholder Advent) voted against his reappointment as Independent Director from May'27
 
Let’s go a bit in history: The company was earlier known as NIIT Tech before its ownership transition & eventual rebranding to Coforge. Barings acquired control of NIIT in 2020, leading to ownership change then.

Later, Barings steadily monetised its stake through multiple block deals as the company scaled in size, profitability & market value. After Barings' complete exit by FY24, Co. become fully public market institutional owned.

OP Bhatt joined the board in 2024 & became Chairman during a phase when Coforge was pursuing aggressive scale-up ambitions. Coforge accelerated inorganic growth. The acquisition of Cigniti significantly expanded its engineering & digital capabilities under him.

The much bigger acquisition Encora was also under OP Bhatt. The acquisition materially increased Coforge's scale, global delivery footprint & exposure to high-growth digital engineering segments.

Encora also changed the shareholding landscape. Through the transaction, Advent became the largest shareholder in Coforge, making its views impossible for the board to ignore. That's why the key takeaway may not be the resignation itself. The bigger story could be that the largest shareholder & the Chairman were not aligned on important matters. 

The bullish view is that management execution remains intact. The cautious view is that whenever Chairman, Board & largest shareholder are not on the same page, governance questions emerge and mgmt. energy is focussed away from growth.

Impact of change in EV subsidy policy from 31 July 2026

PM E-DRIVE subsidy for electric 2Ws ended on 31 Jul 2026. Govt earlier plan was to support E2W till 31 Mar 2026, then gave the industry a 4-month extension till Jul-end as there was unutilized budget

PM E-DRIVE replaced FAME-II in Oct'24 with a 10,900 Cr outlay. The idea was simple: help EV adoption scale while supporting charging infra, buses, trucks & other EV segments

initially, e-2W buyers got subsidy of 5,000/kWh, capped at 10,000/ vehicle. That was a meaningful discount for mass-market scooters. From Apr'25, cut by half to 2,500/kWh with max capped at 5,000/Veh. Signalling gradual withdrawal of support.

Now for 2W, even that 5,000 support is gone. Effective acquisition cost of an EV scooter will move up. 5,000 price hike may not sound huge, but in entry-level its imp for price-sensitive consumer

Some moderation in electric 2W demand was expected. OEMs were preparing for it as subsidy-led growth gradually transitions to product-led growth. 

August EV 2W market share came lower than July. E2W MS has come down but not in 3w as July subsidy withdrawal only 2W not in 3W. August is typically a non-festival month & seasonality also matters. OEMs should absorb subsidy via better exchange / financing offers

Market is also looking for next phase of EV support. Discussions around "FAME III" continue, but indications suggest focus could shift towards vehicle other than 2W. 2W penetration already >10% while other segment need more support

If electric 2Ws are eventually excluded from future demand subsidies, industry economics will increasingly depend on product quality, distribution, service network & battery costs instead of govt incentives.

One factor often ignored: OEMs capacity are planned in a way where capacity expansion will happen in same facility. Hence, incremental capex intensity will be far lower. Gradual drivetrain shift will continue without large incremental capex

Bottom line: Subsidy withdrawal may create short-term demand noise, but the long-term story remains the same. India's 2W market is enormous, EV penetration is still low, and the migration from ICE to EV is likely to be a long, gradual journey rather than a subsidy-driven sprint.

**FCNR Sugar Rush What does it means for India**
FCNR experiment has turned into a blockbuster. Total inflows exceeded $136bn vs market expectations of ~$80bn. FCNR(B) deposits alone ~$127bn
  
Like Hindi movie, climax was amazing. 
Total inflows were ~$41bn by July-end, ~$73bn by Aug 21 and ~$136bn by Aug 31. Biggest forex mobilization drives India has ever seen. August was where the real frenzy happened. FCNR deposits jumped from ~$65.4bn on Aug 21 to ~$127.2bn by Aug 31.
  
Why did NRIs rush in? RBI effectively removed the pain point: currency hedging cost. Banks offered attractive yields while RBI absorbed swap costs For investors, FCNR became a rare risk-reward opportunity. Attractive $ returns + ability to leverage deposits (leverage run 4-5x)
  
FCNR nuance: Depositor takes bank credit risk but avoids INR depreciation risk since deposits remain in foreign currency. Currency mismatch is largely handled by RBI A key incentive for banks: incremental FCNR funds were exempted from CRR & SLR requirements.
  
More deployable money, less regulatory drag hence higher NIMs, Every $ mobilized can potentially earn better spreads for banks Flip side: Liquidity is now overflowing. System liquidity has surged sharply as these inflows entered the banking system

When banks are flush with money, appetite for wholesale funding drops. That's already showing up in lower CD rates & softer short-term funding costs Excess liquidity usually pushes overnight money market rates lower. Too much cash chasing too few opportunities compress yields
 
The RBI also gets a strategic advantage. Larger forex reserves and dollar balances improve its ability to manage forward market positions & reduce pressure from speculative USD demand. Forward dollar short should be reduced going forward
 
For currency speculator, the message is important. Betting aggressively against ₹ becomes tougher when RBI has significantly larger forex ammunition and stronger external buffers Now comes the hard part. Raising $136bn is the easy part.
  
Deploying it productively is the challenge. These are time-bound liabilities with an embedded cost. Eventually the money must earn more than it costs. INR already showing strength: USDINR below 95 today
 
The success of this scheme won't be judged by the $136bn raised. It will be judged by whether India converts this liquidity windfall into stronger growth, stable ₹, lower funding stress & productive credit creation over the next few years
